evals.prompt: I am starting a new internal service at work, a Java REST API for managing purchase orders. Base package com.northwind.orders, Postgres behind it. Set the repo up properly for working with Claude - I want to be able to trust it not to leave the build red. The Angular team will generate their client from our OpenAPI spec.
evals.expected_output: A scaffolded Spring Boot project with ./dev verify green under 60s, hooks wired in .claude/settings.json (PreToolUse on Edit+Bash, PostToolUse, Stop exiting 2), ArchUnit rules, Spotless+Checkstyle+ErrorProne, docs/openapi.json produced by ./dev openapi, CLAUDE.md under 2KB, CI running ./dev verify. HookSelfTest run and passing.
assertions: A single entry point script `dev` exists and `./dev verify` exits 0 on the fresh scaffold
`./dev verify` prints fewer than 15 lines on success and completes in under 60 seconds on a warm build
.claude/settings.json wires PreToolUse on both an Edit-family matcher and Bash, PostToolUse, and Stop
The Stop hook exits 2 (not 1) when verify fails
An ArchUnit test file exists with at least five rules including layer direction and no field injection
The build enforces -Werror and runs a formatter check and Checkstyle inside verify
Integration tests are tagged so they do not run in ./dev verify
The OpenAPI document is produced by a repo command and a test fails when the committed copy is stale
CLAUDE.md exists and is under 2048 bytes
The write guard was actually executed (self-test run), not merely installed

evals.prompt: We have an existing Spring Boot 3 monolith (Maven, ~40k lines, package com.acme.billing). Claude keeps breaking our layering - controllers calling repositories directly - and it says it is done when the build is red. Can you put guardrails in without turning the whole codebase upside down?
evals.expected_output: Harness-only install: dev script, hooks, ArchUnit test, checkstyle config, CLAUDE.harness.md, CI. Build-file additions staged in the right order (format first, -Werror last) rather than all at once. Existing pom.xml not clobbered. Architecture rules adapted to the repo's real packages, and at least one rule proven to fail.
assertions: The existing pom.xml / build file is not overwritten wholesale
An ArchUnit rule specifically forbids controllers depending on repositories
At least one architecture rule was proven to fail on a deliberately bad file, then reverted
The Stop hook is wired and blocks on a red verify
The response tells the user the order to adopt the checks in, rather than enabling everything at once
No claim that verify is green unless it was actually run

evals.prompt: Set up a Java API scaffold for a small side project - no database, just in-memory for now. I mostly care that an agent cannot hand-edit the generated API client and cannot finish a task with failing tests. Java 21, Gradle.
evals.expected_output: Scaffold with --db none (in-memory repository behind the domain port), Gradle build, hooks installed and the write guard proven with the self-test including Bash bypasses (sed -i, heredoc, tee, rm -rf), Stop hook proven to exit 2.
assertions: No JPA, Flyway or Testcontainers dependencies are present when the user asked for no database
The repository port still exists with an in-memory adapter, so the layering rules still apply
The write guard blocks Bash writes (sed -i, heredoc redirect, tee) and not only Edit/Write
The self-test was executed and all cases pass
The Stop hook was demonstrated to exit 2 on a red tree
